findings.title: SQL injection in data migration
findings.body:
The host value `#{h}` is interpolated directly into raw SQL:

  execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"

Any single quote, backslash, or other special character in a legacy `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` value will break the SQL or inject arbitrary statements. A normally configured host like `weird-host's.com` would either corrupt the row or fail the migration entirely; a hostile value (which only an admin could plant, but the surface is the data) could execute arbitrary SQL. Use ActiveRecord's parameterized `EmbeddableHost.create!(host: h, category_id: category_id)` (or bind parameters on `execute`) instead of string interpolation.

findings.title: NoMethodError when no matching category row exists
findings.body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` will raise NoMethodError (`undefined method 'id' for nil`) if the SELECT returns no rows (e.g., the legacy `embed_category` setting was empty, missing, or pointed to a non-existent category name). The `if category_id == 0` guard below only protects against `category_id == 0`; it never runs because the preceding line already raised. Guard against the empty result, e.g. `row = ...; category_id = row && row[0]['id'].to_i`.

findings.title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
findings.body: The callback invokes `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`. If `host` is nil (e.g., a controller passes `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` that is missing or `nil`), `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError before any validation message is generated, producing a 500 instead of a clean 422. Use `self.host.to_s.sub!` or check `self.host.present?` first, and consider switching to non-mutating `gsub` to avoid mutating shared string instances.

findings.title: update action crashes if record lookup returns nil
findings.body: `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil (unknown id), but `save_host(host)` then calls `host.host = ...`, raising NoMethodError on the nil receiver. Either guard with `return render_json_error(...not_found...)` or `save_host` must handle nil. Same problem in `destroy` on line 16: `host.destroy` on nil raises NoMethodError instead of returning a 404.

findings.title: destroy action crashes if record lookup returns nil
findings.body: `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` followed by `host.destroy` raises NoMethodError when no row matches. Should return a 404 (or at least `render_json_error`) when the record cannot be found, matching REST expectations.

findings.title: save_host assumes nested params without guarding
findings.body: `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` raise NoMethodError when a non-nested request body or an unrelated shape is sent. Wrapping with `params.require(:embeddable_host).permit(:host, :category_id)` (or a `params[:embeddable_host].present?` guard) would convert the request into a clean 400 with the existing error rendering path.

findings.title: PUT endpoint never persists anything
findings.body: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders the existing `@embedding` OpenStruct without reading any attributes or persisting any change. Combined with the `saveChanges` JS action that has no template binding, this endpoint is effectively a no-op dressed as a save. Either remove the route/action or have it accept and persist the submitted payload. As written it silently swallows PUTs, which could mask a real bug later when UI starts exercising it.

findings.title: Spec only asserts inheritance, not behavior
findings.body: The new controller's `create`, `update`, and `destroy` actions have no tests at all - not even happy-path coverage, param shape validation, or auth checks. The two bugs above (nil record lookup, missing nested params) would have been caught by minimal request specs. Add specs that POST/PUT/DELETE with valid and invalid ids and shapes.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents swapped from filename
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` while every category-shaped fabricator (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) was moved to the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. The file containing the category fabricators is named for a different model, so anyone editing tests for categories will be looking in the wrong place. The contents should be restored so the file naming matches what it actually defines.

findings.title: edit action reads id off possibly-missing category
findings.body: `this.set('categoryId', this.get('host.category.id'))` crashes when `host.category` is undefined. For the standard pencil flow on existing rows `category` is hydrated server-side, but if category hydration ever fails (e.g., category deleted, rest serializer misconfigured) the entire component breaks. Use `(this.get('host.category') || {}).id` or a helper to read safely.

findings.title: pathFor silently ignores findArgs/id
findings.body: The custom `pathFor` returns the hard-coded `/admin/customize/embedding` and drops any `findArgs`/`id` argument. It currently happens to work because both `find` and `update` resolve to that single route, but anything that legitimately wants to send an id (e.g., a future destroy/update-by-id, or even just `findAll`) will go to the wrong URL with no diagnostic. Either extend `pathFor` to handle arguments properly or add a comment documenting the intentional limitation.

findings.title: Removed method leaves config/locales blank
findings.body: Both `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` translations and YAML keys were removed in tandem with the model method, but the old JSON-API style removal comment is not present and there is no migration comment explaining the data movement. The shipped migration file (20150818190757) does the data backfill, which is good, but anyone running an out-of-order deploy against an already-migrated DB will simply lose both settings with no diagnostic. Consider also handling the setting rows on initial run rather than only in `change`.
